capture_engagement.description: Whether the engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) of the email your code rendered are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says.

description.description: Notes about which emails belong to the category. Recipients don't see it.

key.description: The category's key, unique within the project, such as `newsletter`. Opt-outs and the preferences page refer to the category by it.

name.description: The category's name, shown in the PostHog app. Used only when the send creates the category: rename it in the app.

type.description: `marketing`: recipients can opt out, and the send skips those who did. `transactional`: for email a recipient must get, which skips opt-outs.

category.description: Message category of the email. Leave it out or send `transactional` for a transactional email with no category, which skips opt-outs. Or define the category in code with `key`, `type`, `name` and an optional `description`. The send creates the category when the project has none with that key, and restores it when it was archived. It never changes an existing category's name or description. An existing category must have the same `type`. A `marketing` email skips recipients who opted out of its category or of all marketing, gets unsubscribe headers, and can't have `cc` or `bcc`. Its `html` needs a link whose `href` is `{{ unsubscribe_url }}`, or its `text` needs `{{ unsubscribe_url }}` when it has no `html`. PostHog replaces the placeholder with the recipient's unsubscribe link. A send with `template_id`, or with a `template_key` that names a template, follows the template's category: leave it out there, or send the template's own.

distinct_id.description: Distinct ID of the recipient's person. The send and its engagement events are recorded against that person. Defaults to the recipient's email address.

from.description: Sender of the email your code rendered, as `security@example.com` or `Example <security@example.com>`, on a verified domain of the project. Without it, the email goes out from the project's default sender, or from its only verified sender when it has no default.

html.description: HTML body of the email, exactly as the recipient should see it. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB, and quotes and line breaks count twice. A larger email can't be sent here.

reply_to.description: Addresses replies to the email your code rendered go to.

subject.description: Subject of the email your code rendered.

template_key.description: Names an email whose content your code rendered, such as `order-shipped`, so its metrics, logs and status group under it. Letters, numbers, hyphens (-) and underscores (_) only, at most 256 characters. Send it with `subject` and `html` or `text`. PostHog sends the content as is and never stores it as a template.

text.description: Plain text body of the email. Without it, PostHog derives the text from html. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB.
